title: ICE external-comparator choice-robustness protocol
description: A non-authoritative, design-only route for separating implementation calibration, modified-gravity comparison, and folded-seam classification. It records no computation, observation, claim, or canonical-graph change.

selected_strategy.rationale: First establish a declared JBD reference-limit calibration, then audit a fixed Hu-Sawicki n=1 comparator across independently defined consumers. Any later ICE admission remains conditional on a specified action and invariant observables; folded-seam classification is explicitly parallel rather than a premise or corroboration.

models.name: Jordan-Brans-Dicke declared GR-limit calibration
models.action: S_JBD=(16 pi)^-1 int d^4x sqrt(-g)[Phi R-omega_BD Phi^-1 (nabla Phi)^2-2 V(Phi)]+S_m[g,psi], with V(Phi) fixed before comparison.
models.convention: Metric signature, Riemann sign, action normalization, Jordan-frame matter coupling, and scalar boundary conditions are fixed in the planned input ledger.
models.parameter_lock: One declared omega_BD trajectory, potential choice, background parameters, and GR-limit prescription; no post-comparison retuning.
models.matter_coupling: Universal minimally coupled matter in the declared Jordan frame only.
models.boundary_domain: Calibration is limited to the stated action, branch, boundary conditions, and reference-limit observables.
models.non_claim: Reproducing a reference limit would test implementation fidelity only; it would not support ICE or establish a new gravitational mechanism.

models.name: Hu-Sawicki metric f(R) n=1 comparator
models.action: S=int d^4x sqrt(-g)[(R+f_HS(R))/(2 kappa^2)+L_m], with f_HS(R)=-m^2 c1(R/m^2)/[c2(R/m^2)+1] for n=1; the scalar degree of freedom and high-curvature branch are declared model content.
models.convention: Metric variation, f_R definition, curvature sign, action normalization, and the mapping between c1, c2 and f_R0 are frozen before any comparison.
models.parameter_lock: One n=1 branch, one stated f_R0 or equivalent c1/c2 value, one background parameter set, and one screening/environment prescription across all consumers.
models.matter_coupling: Matter coupling and environmental screening assumptions are stated as part of the comparator, not imported from ICE.
models.boundary_domain: Only the declared metric-variation n=1 model and viability branch are compared; no generic f(R), JBD equivalence, or matter-geometrization conclusion follows.
models.non_claim: This candidate comparator is not an ICE action and a fit in one consumer would not establish a common mechanism.

models.name: Folded Wess-Zumino seam classification comparator
models.action: A local Wess-Zumino comparator with a separately declared seam or sheet label, used only to classify whether a proposed operation is a fermion-odd supercharge or a distinct sewing map.
models.convention: Specify the Hilbert-space domain, grading, complex-linearity, charge adjoint, and seam boundary data before classification.
models.parameter_lock: One fixed local multiplet and one seam operation; no tuning of a mass spectrum, state occupation, or sheet basis after classification.
models.matter_coupling: No cosmological matter coupling is inferred; this is an algebraic/domain classification only.
models.boundary_domain: The comparison is limited to operator typing and domain compatibility and does not construct a physical CPT/Pin sewing or a persistent interacting splitting.
models.non_claim: A successful algebraic classification would not establish a physical cross-sheet charge, common positive product, or phenomenological signal.

consumers.observable: Declared dimensionless background expansion relation H(z)/H0 on the fixed background parameter set.
consumers.independence_boundary: Background distance/expansion information is not reused as a scalar perturbation or tensor observable.
consumers.non_claim: Agreement in this one consumer alone is not a modified-gravity mechanism or ICE evidence.

consumers.observable: Declared linear scalar growth and lensing/slip relation computed from the same frozen action and parameter set.
consumers.independence_boundary: This is a scalar perturbation consumer distinct from the background relation and must not be replaced by a re-expression of it.
consumers.non_claim: A scalar-sector pattern is not independent if it is produced by separately retuned functions or an unmatched screening prescription.

consumers.observable: Declared linear tensor propagation relation from the same frozen action, matter coupling, and branch.
consumers.independence_boundary: Tensor propagation is a separately defined sector, not a transformed scalar or background residual.
consumers.non_claim: No tensor prediction, propagation anomaly, or data comparison is asserted by this planned consumer.

steps.title: Lock and calibrate the declared JBD GR-limit reference

inputs.specification: A frozen JBD action, omega_BD trajectory, potential choice, matter coupling, boundary conditions, units, and GR-limit prescription.

outputs.specification: A pass/fail specification for reference-limit agreement under the declared conventions; it contains no computed value.

choice_dimensions: Jordan versus Einstein-frame bookkeeping with transformed matter coupling
steps.mechanism_object: The declared scalar-tensor reference-limit observable class, not a coordinate-dependent scalar value.
steps.parameter_lock: The convention ledger is frozen before any calibration comparison.
steps.independent_check: A transformed-frame derivation is admissible only when the matter coupling and boundary map are carried with it.
steps.acceptance_criterion: A future calibration may be called implementation-consistent only if both declared formulations reproduce the same reference-limit observable within predeclared numerical control.
steps.null_outcome: Failure to match the reference limit leaves the implementation uncalibrated and supplies no model comparison.
steps.kill_criterion: Any apparent agreement that requires changing the potential, boundary conditions, matter coupling, or parameter path after inspection kills the calibration interpretation.
steps.non_claim: This is not an ICE calculation or evidence that JBD is realized in nature.

steps.title: Audit the locked Hu-Sawicki n=1 comparator definition

inputs.specification: A fixed n=1 functional form, f_R convention, f_R0 or c1/c2 conversion, background parameters, branch, and screening/environment assumptions.

outputs.specification: A convention-complete list of equations, degrees of freedom, branch constraints, and observable mappings to be checked before a cross-domain comparison.

steps.mechanism_object: The n=1 metric f(R) scalar mode and its fixed action-level coupling relations.
steps.parameter_lock: All parameter conversions and branch conditions are fixed before any consumer is evaluated.
steps.independent_check: Derive the declared scalar-tensor representation only with its stated assumptions and compare invariant observables rather than bare field names.
steps.acceptance_criterion: The planned cross-domain test is admitted only when one unambiguous convention and parameter ledger maps to every listed consumer.
steps.null_outcome: Ambiguous parameterization, branch, or matter coupling leaves the model comparison unresolved.
steps.kill_criterion: If the required observable mapping changes with an undeclared reparameterization or distinct boundary condition, do not call the comparator choice-robust.
steps.non_claim: This audit does not derive Hu-Sawicki dynamics from ICE and does not test data.

steps.title: Specify a same-coupling Hu-Sawicki n=1 cross-domain test

inputs.specification: The same locked n=1 action, parameters, initial conditions, branch, matter coupling, and observable definitions for background, scalar growth/lensing, and tensor propagation.

outputs.specification: A future matched-formulation protocol with declared invariance, null, and independence conditions; no solver has been installed or run.

steps.mechanism_object: One frozen action-level coupling set connecting the three independently defined consumers.
steps.parameter_lock: No consumer receives a separately fitted parameter, nuisance function, branch, or screening rule.
steps.independent_check: After installation is separately approved, compare independently maintained H-EFTCAMB and hi_class implementations only under independently audited action-to-code maps, identical declared inputs, and identical observable conventions; an adapter error common to both is not excluded.
steps.acceptance_criterion: A future effect is eligible for comparator-level robustness review only if it survives admissible formulation changes and the same locked coupling reaches at least two independent consumers.
steps.null_outcome: A stable GR-limit or absence of a correlated deviation is a valid null comparator outcome.
steps.kill_criterion: Retuning per consumer, unmatched initial/boundary conditions, solver-only agreement, or a single-domain fit kills the common-mechanism interpretation.
steps.non_claim: No tool is installed, no computation or likelihood is planned by this record, and no ICE prediction is asserted.

steps.title: Specify an ICE geometry-route admission decision

inputs.specification: A proposed fundamental configuration object, covariant action, gauge redundancy, boundary/variational domain, degrees of freedom, matter coupling, and invariant observable map.

outputs.specification: A human-review criterion stating what would be needed to distinguish a new ICE action from an effective-fluid relabeling or an existing comparator class.

steps.mechanism_object: A future explicitly typed ICE action-to-invariant-observable map; it is absent from this design record.
steps.parameter_lock: No ICE parameter exists here; admission requires one predeclared action and coupling set before any comparison.
steps.independent_check: An ICE candidate would require an independently audited analytic formulation and numerical implementation plus two in-programme consumers, not a comparison to a single f(R) fit.
steps.acceptance_criterion: Only a future specified action with a choice-invariant observable distinction and same-mechanism multi-consumer fingerprint could be admitted for bounded review.
steps.null_outcome: If the proposed difference is only an equation-side move, field redefinition, or comparator reparameterization, retain an equivalent-description or unresolved classification.
steps.kill_criterion: Missing action, degree-of-freedom accounting, boundary domain, matter coupling, or invariant observable distinction forbids ICE-model admission.
steps.non_claim: This is not an ICE candidate claim, a canonical open problem, or a dependency of any CPT gate or P7 likelihood lane.

steps.title: Classify a folded Wess-Zumino seam without conflating it with CPT sewing

inputs.specification: A fixed local multiplet, seam operation, grading, common domain, adjoint, complex-linearity, and CPT/Pin operator type.

outputs.specification: A future yes/no operator-typing criterion distinguishing a fermion-odd supercharge from a separate sewing map.

steps.mechanism_object: The explicitly typed operator and common-domain relation, not a sheet-mixing matrix alone.
steps.parameter_lock: The local multiplet, operator grading, and seam conditions are fixed before classification.
steps.independent_check: Compare operator grading and adjoint/domain properties in a separately written representation without identifying CPT/Pin with Q.
steps.acceptance_criterion: A future classification is internally consistent only if the fermion-odd charge and the CPT/Pin sewing operation remain separately typed and domain-compatible.
steps.null_outcome: A seam that changes state data but does not define a physical fermion-odd charge remains a scoped null classification.
steps.kill_criterion: Basis-only mixing, absent common positive domain, or conflation of anti-linear sewing with a fermion-odd supercharge kills the classification interpretation.
steps.non_claim: This contextualizes the existing Gate 4 question non-authoritatively only; it is neither its prerequisite nor evidence for it, and has no geometry-lane dependency.

boundaries: This protocol is non-authoritative design only and changes no canonical ontology graph, claim, evidence state, gate, planner, or execution authorization.
Geometry-comparator steps carry no CPT context reference and do not target Gate 1, P7, legacy predictions, or any likelihood route.

The only CPT context is the folded classification step's non-authoritative contextual reference to open:gate4-spinorial-charge-domain-constraint-closure; it is not evidence, a prerequisite, or a dependency.

No tool is installed and no execution, solver output, likelihood, observation, calibration outcome, or model-selection conclusion is recorded.
